``` {r temp chat mapping}
# Packages 
# install these only once
# install.packages(c("sf","ggplot2","readxl","ggmap","ggspatial", "terra", "geodata", "tidyterra", "raster", "svglite"))

library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(readxl)
library(ggmap)     # for get_stadia_map()
library(ggspatial)
library(raster) # only for the coordinate grid, optional
library(svglite)
library(terra)
library(geodata)
library(tidyterra)

# fetch & cache a single background raster

get_cached_map <- function(bbox, zoom = 12, maptype = "terrain-background",
                           cache_file = file.path(tempdir(), "cached_map.rds")) {
  # Return cached file if it exists
  if (file.exists(cache_file)) {
    message("Re‑using cached map: ", cache_file)
    return(readRDS(cache_file))
  }

  # Download a fresh raster from Stadia
  message("Downloading Stadia map …")
  # ggmap expects bbox as c(left,bottom,right,top)
  stadia_bbox <- c(bbox[1], bbox[2], bbox[3], bbox[4])

  map_raster <- get_stadiamap(bbox = stadia_bbox,
                               zoom = zoom,
                               maptype = maptype)   # class 'ggmap'

  # Persist for future runs
  message("Map cached to: ", cache_file)
  saveRDS(map_raster, cache_file)
  map_raster
}

# Load three data frames

insect_locate        <- read_excel("insect_presence_no_damage_LatLong.xlsx")
damage_insect_locate <- read_excel("insect_presence_damage_LatLong.xlsx")
damage_locate        <- read_excel("no_insect_damage_presence_LatLong.xlsx")


# Convert to "simple features" (sf) and add a “type” column 

insects_sf  <- st_as_sf(insect_locate,    coords = c("longitude","latitude"), crs = 4326)
insects_sf$type  <- "insect_presence"

damage_sf   <- st_as_sf(damage_insect_locate,coords = c("longitude","latitude"), crs = 4326)
damage_sf$type <- "damage_and_insect"

nodamage_sf <- st_as_sf(damage_locate,    coords = c("longitude","latitude"), crs = 4326)
nodamage_sf$type <- "damage_but_no_insect"


# Combine all sf's into a single sf object

all_pts <- rbind(insects_sf, damage_sf, nodamage_sf)

all_pts <- rbind(insects_sf, damage_sf, nodamage_sf)
all_pts <- all_pts[!st_is_empty(all_pts), ]   # drop empty geometries


# Optional geometry simplification for speed 

crs_proj <- 5070  # NAD83 / UTM zone 15N – good for continental US
all_pts  <- st_transform(all_pts, crs = crs_proj)
all_pts  <- st_simplify(all_pts, dTolerance = 21, preserveTopology = TRUE)
all_pts  <- st_transform(all_pts, crs = 4326)   # back to WGS‑84

#option to jitter points (not used)
#jitter_amount <- 3e-04                # ≈ 30m in degrees
#jittered_all_pts <- st_jitter(all_pts, factor = jitter_amount)


# Tight bounding box + small buffer 
bbox <- st_bbox(all_pts)
lon_buffer <- diff(c(bbox$xmin, bbox$xmax)) * 0.05
lat_buffer <- diff(c(bbox$ymin, bbox$ymax)) * 0.05

bbox_vec <- c(
  xmin = bbox$xmin - lon_buffer,
  ymin = bbox$ymin - lat_buffer,
  xmax = bbox$xmax + lon_buffer,
  ymax = bbox$ymax + lat_buffer
)

bbox_vec <- c(
  xmin = unname(bbox$xmin - lon_buffer),
  ymin = unname(bbox$ymin - lat_buffer),
  xmax = unname(bbox$xmax + lon_buffer),
  ymax = unname(bbox$ymax + lat_buffer)
)

print(bbox_vec)


# Fetch (or reuse) the cached background raster 

clim_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "worldclim")
dir.create(clim_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Remove the bad zip/cache so geodata is forced to re-download cleanly
unlink(clim_dir, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(clim_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Increase timeout - default is 60s, way too short for ~800MB file
options(timeout = 600)  # 10 minutes

#increase or decrease resolution depending on needs and size of map/display area
bioclim <- worldclim_global(var = "bio", res = 2.5, path = clim_dir)
# Layer 1 of the bioclim stack = BIO1 = Annual Mean Temperature (°C)
temp_annual <- bioclim[["wc2.1_2.5m_bio_1"]]



# Crop/mask to your study area bounding box 
crop_ext <- ext(bbox_vec["xmin"], bbox_vec["xmax"],
                 bbox_vec["ymin"], bbox_vec["ymax"])

temp_crop <- crop(temp_annual, crop_ext)
names(temp_crop) <- "avg_temp_C"

# Plot 

p <- ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = temp_crop) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = c("#2c7bb6", "#abd9e9", "#ffffbf", "#fdae61", "#d7191c"),
    name = "Avg. Annual\nTemp (°C)",
    na.value = NA
  ) +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_color() +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
  geom_sf(data = all_pts,
          aes(shape = type, color = type),
          size = 3, alpha = 0.9, stroke = 0.5) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("insect_presence" = 0,
                                 "damage_and_insect"    = 1,
                                 "damage_but_no_insect" = 2),
                      labels = c("insect_presence" = "Arthropod Present",
                                 "damage_and_insect"    = "Arthropod and Damage Present",
                                 "damage_but_no_insect" = "Damage but no Arthropod")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("insect_presence" = "black",
                                 "damage_and_insect"    = "black",
                                 "damage_but_no_insect" = "black"),
                      labels = c("insect_presence" = "Arthropod Present",
                                 "damage_and_insect"    = "Arthropod and Damage Present",
                                 "damage_but_no_insect" = "Damage but no Arthropod")) +
  labs(shape = "Key:", color = "Key:") +
  theme_minimal() +
  coord_sf(xlim = bbox_vec[c(1,3)],
           ylim = bbox_vec[c(2,4)],
           expand = FALSE,
           crs = st_crs(4326),
           default_crs = st_crs(4326)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.box = "vertical")

ggsave("insect_damage_temperature_map.png", plot = p, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
ggsave("insect_damage_temperature_map.svg", plot = p, width = 8, height = 6)
```

``` {r SE regional temp chat mapping}
  labs(shape = "Key:", color = "Key:") +
  theme_minimal() +
  coord_sf(xlim = bbox_vec[c(1,3)],
```

``` {r PNW regional temp chat mapping}
# Load in the three data frames
insect_locate        <- read_excel("W_insect_presence_no_damage_LatLong.xlsx")
damage_insect_locate <- read_excel("W_insect_presence_damage_LatLong.xlsx")

# Convert to sf and add a “type” column 
insects_sf  <- st_as_sf(insect_locate,    coords = c("longitude","latitude"), crs = 4326)
insects_sf$type  <- "insect_presence"

damage_sf   <- st_as_sf(damage_insect_locate,coords = c("longitude","latitude"), crs = 4326)
damage_sf$type <- "damage_and_insect"

nodamage_sf <- st_as_sf(damage_locate,    coords = c("longitude","latitude"), crs = 4326)
nodamage_sf$type <- "damage_but_no_insect"

# Combine into a single sf object
all_pts <- rbind(insects_sf, damage_sf, nodamage_sf)

all_pts <- rbind(insects_sf, damage_sf, nodamage_sf)
all_pts <- all_pts[!st_is_empty(all_pts), ]   # drop empty geometries

# Optional geometry simplification for speed 
crs_proj <- 5070  # NAD83 / UTM zone 15N – good for continental US
all_pts  <- st_transform(all_pts, crs = crs_proj)
all_pts  <- st_simplify(all_pts, dTolerance = 21, preserveTopology = TRUE)
all_pts  <- st_transform(all_pts, crs = 4326)   # back to WGS‑84

#jitter_amount <- 3e-04                # ≈ 30m in degrees
#jittered_all_pts <- st_jitter(all_pts, factor = jitter_amount)

# Tight bounding box + small buffer
bbox <- st_bbox(all_pts)
lon_buffer <- diff(c(bbox$xmin, bbox$xmax)) * 0.05
lat_buffer <- diff(c(bbox$ymin, bbox$ymax)) * 0.05

bbox_vec <- c(
  xmin = bbox$xmin - lon_buffer,
  ymin = bbox$ymin - lat_buffer,
  xmax = bbox$xmax + lon_buffer,
  ymax = bbox$ymax + lat_buffer
)

bbox_vec <- c(
  xmin = unname(bbox$xmin - lon_buffer),
  ymin = unname(bbox$ymin - lat_buffer),
  xmax = unname(bbox$xmax + lon_buffer),
  ymax = unname(bbox$ymax + lat_buffer)
)

print(bbox_vec)

#  Fetch (or reuse) the cached background raster 
                 
clim_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "worldclim")
dir.create(clim_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Remove the bad zip/cache so geodata is forced to re-download cleanly
unlink(clim_dir, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(clim_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Increase timeout - default is 60s, way too short for ~800MB file
options(timeout = 600)  # 10 minutes

# res options: 10, 5, 2.5, 0.5 (arc-minutes). Smaller = finer but bigger download.
# For a tight regional bbox, 0.5 (~1km) gives much better detail than 2.5.
bioclim <- worldclim_global(var = "bio", res = 2.5, path = clim_dir)
# Layer 1 of the bioclim stack = BIO1 = Annual Mean Temperature (°C)
temp_annual <- bioclim[["wc2.1_2.5m_bio_1"]]



# Crop/mask to your study area bounding box 
crop_ext <- ext(bbox_vec["xmin"], bbox_vec["xmax"],
                 bbox_vec["ymin"], bbox_vec["ymax"])

temp_crop <- crop(temp_annual, crop_ext)
names(temp_crop) <- "avg_temp_C"

# Plot

p <- ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = temp_crop) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = c("#2c7bb6", "#abd9e9", "#ffffbf"),
    name = "Avg. Annual\nTemp (°C)",
    na.value = NA
  ) +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_color() +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
  geom_sf(data = all_pts,
          aes(shape = type, color = type),
          size = 3, alpha = 0.9, stroke = 0.5) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("insect_presence" = 0,
                                 "damage_and_insect"    = 1,
                                 "damage_but_no_insect" = 2),
                      labels = c("insect_presence" = "Arthropod Present",
                                 "damage_and_insect"    = "Arthropod and Damage Present",
                                 "damage_but_no_insect" = "Damage but no Arthropod")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("insect_presence" = "black",
                                 "damage_and_insect"    = "black",
                                 "damage_but_no_insect" = "black"),
                      labels = c("insect_presence" = "Arthropod Present",
                                 "damage_and_insect"    = "Arthropod and Damage Present",
                                 "damage_but_no_insect" = "Damage but no Arthropod")) +
  labs(shape = "Key:", color = "Key:") +
  theme_minimal() +
  coord_sf(xlim = bbox_vec[c(1,3)],
           ylim = bbox_vec[c(2,4)],
           expand = FALSE,
           crs = st_crs(4326),
           default_crs = st_crs(4326)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.box = "vertical")

p <- p +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 3)) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9))

ggsave("PNW_insect_damage_temperature_map.png", plot = p, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
ggsave("PNW_insect_damage_temperature_map.svg", plot = p, width = 8, height = 6)
```

```{r piechart}
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

df <- read_excel("presence_damage_occurencesV2.xlsx")

pie_df <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(In_contact), !is.na(damaged)) %>%
  mutate(
    category = case_when(
      In_contact == 0 & damaged == 0 ~ "No arthropod or damage",
      In_contact == 1 & damaged == 0 ~ "Arthropod present",
      In_contact == 1 & damaged == 1 ~ "Arthropod and damage present",
      In_contact == 0 & damaged == 1 ~ "Damage but no arthropod"
    ),
    category = factor(category, levels = c(
      "Arthropod present",
      "Arthropod and damage present",
      "Damage but no arthropod",
      "No arthropod or damage"
    ))
  ) %>%
  count(category, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(
    fraction = n / sum(n),
    ymax = cumsum(fraction),
    ymin = c(0, head(ymax, -1)),
    label_pos = (ymin + ymax) / 2,
    label = paste0(category, "\nn=", n)
  )

presence_colors_cb <- c(
  "Arthropod present"             = "#56B4E9",
  "Arthropod and damage present"  = "#009E73",
  "Damage but no arthropod"       = "#E69F00",
  "No arthropod or damage"        = "#999999"
)

pie_df <- pie_df %>%
  mutate(
    # x = radius: smaller = closer to the ring, larger = farther out
    label_x = case_when(
      category == "Arthropod present"            ~ 3.0,
      category == "Arthropod and damage present"  ~ 4.3,
      category == "Damage but no arthropod"       ~ 4.5,
      category == "No arthropod or damage"  ~ 3.1,
      TRUE                                        ~ 2.6
    ),
    # y = angle position: nudging this shifts a label left/right around the circle
    label_y = case_when(
      category == "Arthropod present"            ~ label_pos - 0.02,
      category == "Arthropod and damage present"  ~ label_pos + 0.12,
      category == "Damage but no arthropod"  ~ label_pos + 0.06,
      category == "No arthropod or damage"  ~ label_pos + -0.13,
      TRUE                                        ~ label_pos
    )
  )
#highly recommend just moving labels in Figma or photoshop, that^ was awful

damage_presence_pie <- ggplot(pie_df, aes(x = 2, y = fraction, fill = category)) +
  geom_col(width = 1, color = "white", position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y", start = -pi/6) +
  xlim(0.5, 6.5) +
  geom_text(aes(x = label_x, y = label_y, label = label, color = category),
            size = 3.2, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE, lineheight = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = presence_colors_cb) +
  scale_color_manual(values = presence_colors_cb) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

ggsave("damage_presence_pie.png", plot = damage_presence_pie, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
ggsave("damage_presence_pie.svg", plot = damage_presence_pie, width = 8, height = 6)

```

```{r COFsunburst}
# ============================================================
# Publication-quality taxonomic sunburst with class, order, and family
# ============================================================

# Install these once if necessary:
# install.packages(c("readr", "dplyr", "plotly", "colorspace", "htmlwidgets"))

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(plotly)
library(colorspace)
library(htmlwidgets)


# READ DATA

df <- read_csv("contact_COF_v2.csv",
               show_col_types = FALSE)


#  ASSIGN TAXONOMIC RANKS

ranks <- c(
  "class",
  "order",
  "family"
)


# CLEAN TAXONOMIC NAMES

clean_taxon <- function(x) {

  x <- trimws(as.character(x))

  x[
    is.na(x) |
    x == "" |
    tolower(x) %in% c(
      "unknown",
      "unidentified",
      "na",
      "n/a",
      "none",
      "null"
    )
  ] <- NA

  x
}

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(ranks),
      clean_taxon
    )
  )


# GIVE EACH OBSERVATION A COUNT OF 1

df$count <- 1


#  FUNCTION TO CREATE EACH TAXONOMIC LEVEL

make_level <- function(data, rank, parent_ranks) {

  # Need the current rank
  required <- c(parent_ranks, rank)

  data %>%
    filter(
      if_all(
        all_of(required),
        ~ !is.na(.)
      )
    ) %>%
    group_by(
      across(all_of(required))
    ) %>%
    summarise(
      value = sum(count),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%

    # Create unique ID for each taxon
    mutate(
      id = apply(
        select(., all_of(required)),
        1,
        paste,
        collapse = "|"
      ),

      # Parent is everything except current rank
      parent = if (length(parent_ranks) == 0) {
        ""
      } else {
        apply(
          select(., all_of(parent_ranks)),
          1,
          paste,
          collapse = "|"
        )
      },

      label = .data[[rank]],

      rank = rank
    ) %>%

    select(
      id,
      label,
      parent,
      value,
      rank
    )
}


#  CREATE EACH TAXONOMIC LEVEL

class_data <- make_level(
  df,
  "class",
  character(0)
)

order_data <- make_level(
  df,
  "order",
  "class"
)

family_data <- make_level(
  df,
  "family",
  c("class", "order")
)



#  COMBINE EVERYTHING

plot_data <- bind_rows(
  class_data,
  order_data,
  family_data,
)


#  CREATE COLOR PALETTE

# Colorblind-friendly palette
base_colors <- c(
  "#0072B2",  # blue
  "#E69F00",  # orange
  "#009E73",  # green
  "#CC79A7",  # purple
  "#D55E00",  # vermillion
  "#332288",  # sky blue
  "#DDCC77",  # yellow
  "#E7180B",  # wine
  "#44AA99",  # teal
  "#F0E442",  # violet
  "#AA4499",  # dark green
  "#117733",  # sand
  "#56B4E9",  # dark blue
  "#D42288",  # pink
  "#008067"   # green-teal
)


#  ASSIGN EACH ORDER A COLOR

order_names <- unique(
  plot_data$label[
    plot_data$rank == "order"
  ]
)

# Assign one base color to each order
order_colors <- setNames(
  base_colors[
    seq_len(length(order_names))
  ],
  order_names
)


# DETERMINE WHICH ORDER EACH TAXON BELONGS TO

plot_data <- plot_data %>%
  mutate(
    major_group = case_when(

      # Class level has no order yet
      rank == "class" ~ label,

      # Order level
      rank == "order" ~ label,

      # Family level: order is second component of ID
      rank == "family" ~ sapply(
        strsplit(id, "\\|"),
        function(x) x[2]
      )
    )
  )


#  ASSIGN COLORS & HOVER INFORMATION

plot_data <- plot_data %>%
  mutate(

    # Assign colors
    color = case_when(

      # Class ring gets a neutral gray
      rank == "class" ~ "#BDBDBD",

      # Orders get their assigned base color
      rank == "order" ~ unname(
        order_colors[major_group]
      ),

      # Families get a lighter version of their order
      rank == "family" ~ lighten(
        unname(order_colors[major_group]),
        amount = 0.35
      )
    ),

    # Hover information
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", label, "</b>",
      "<br>Rank: ", rank,
      "<br>Observations: ", value
    )
  )

# CREATE THE SUNBURST PLOT

fig <- plot_ly(
  data = plot_data,

  ids = ~id,
  labels = ~label,
  parents = ~parent,
  values = ~value,

  type = "sunburst",

  branchvalues = "total",

  marker = list(
    colors = plot_data$color,
    line = list(
      color = "white",
      width = 1
    )
  ),

  hovertext = ~hover_text,
  hoverinfo = "text",

  insidetextorientation = "radial",

  maxdepth = 6
)


#  FIGURE APPEARANCE

fig <- fig %>%
  layout(
    margin = list(
      l = 10,
      r = 10,
      b = 10,
      t = 10
    ),

    paper_bgcolor = "white",

    font = list(
      family = "Arial",
      size = 12
    )
  )


fig


# SAVE INTERACTIVE HTML

saveWidget(
  fig,
  "sunburst_figure5.html",
  selfcontained = TRUE
)

```

```{krona}

#####python code to convert raw .csv identification data into a count .tsv
import pandas as pd

# Input/output files
INPUT_FILE = "contact_classifications.csv"   # actually an Excel file
OUTPUT_FILE = "krona_input.tsv"

# Minimum abundance to keep
MIN_COUNT = 1        # change to 2 or 3 to remove singletons

# Read file
df = pd.read_excel(INPUT_FILE)

taxonomy_cols = [
    "phylum",
    "class",
    "order",
    "family",
    "genus",
    "species"
]

# Clean taxonomy
def clean_taxon(x):
    if pd.isna(x):
        return ""

    x = str(x).strip()

    if x.lower() in {
        "",
        "unknown",
        "unidentified",
        "na",
        "n/a",
        "none",
        "nan"
    }:
        return ""

    return x

for col in taxonomy_cols:
    df[col] = df[col].apply(clean_taxon)

# Add higher taxonomy
domain = []
kingdom = []

for phylum in df["phylum"]:

    # Arthropods
    if phylum == "Hexapoda":
        domain.append("Eukaryota")
        kingdom.append("Animalia")

    elif phylum == "Arthropoda":
        domain.append("Eukaryota")
        kingdom.append("Animalia")

    # Fungi
    elif phylum in [
        "Ascomycota",
        "Basidiomycota",
        "Mucoromycota",
        "Glomeromycota"
    ]:
        domain.append("Eukaryota")
        kingdom.append("Fungi")

    else:
        domain.append("Eukaryota")
        kingdom.append("Other")

df.insert(0, "domain", domain)
df.insert(1, "kingdom", kingdom)

taxonomy = ["domain", "kingdom"] + taxonomy_cols

# Collapse identical classifications
counts = (
    df.groupby(taxonomy)
      .size()
      .reset_index(name="count")
)

# Remove rare taxa if desired
counts = counts[counts["count"] >= MIN_COUNT]

# Remove blank ranks from each row
rows = []

for _, row in counts.iterrows():

    lineage = [str(row["count"])]

    for rank in taxonomy:
        if row[rank] != "":
            lineage.append(row[rank])

    rows.append(lineage)

# Write Krona input
with open(OUTPUT_FILE, "w") as out:

    for lineage in rows:
        out.write("\t".join(lineage) + "\n")

print(f"Wrote {OUTPUT_FILE}")
print(f"{len(rows)} unique taxonomic paths.")


#####python code to run in terminal to generate krona plot:
ktImportText krona_input.tsv -o contact_classifications_krona.html

```
